issues.failure_explanation:
The proof of Theorem 7 claims that the quadratic form a(u,u) = \int_B (D |
abla(\phi u)|^2 + \epsilon^{-2} D (1-\phi) |u|^2) dx is identical (up to epsilon scaling) to DDM1, where the gradient term is \int_B \phi D |
abla u|^2 dx. However, |
abla(\phi u)|^2 is not equal to \phi |
abla u|^2. Furthermore, coercivity a(u,u) >= c \|u\|^2 does not hold for the stated norm \|u\|^2 = \int_B (\phi |
abla u|^2 + \epsilon^{-2}(1-\phi)u^2) dx: for high-frequency oscillatory functions u_k(x) = \sin(k x_1) \psi(x) supported in a subregion where \phi(x) <= \delta, |
abla(\phi u_k)|^2 scales as k^2 \phi^2 whereas \phi |
abla u_k|^2 scales as k^2 \phi, causing the ratio a(u_k, u_k) / \|u_k\|^2 to tend to at most O(\delta) as k -> \infty, which can be made arbitrarily small.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the energy norm associated with SBM to \|u\|_{SBM}^2 := \int_B (|\nabla(\phi u)|^2 + \epsilon^{-2}(1-\phi)|u|^2) dx, show that \|u\|_{SBM} defines a norm on H^1_0(B), and establish coercivity with respect to this SBM-specific norm.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 7 (coercivity of SBM) is unsupported and false for the claimed norm. Theorem 16 (coercivity of SBM with advection) directly relies on Theorem 7 for coercivity of the diffusion operator and is therefore also invalidated.
issues.title: Invalid coercivity proof and false coercivity claim for SBM
issues.why_classification: A complete resolution is achieved by adopting the natural norm \|u\|_{SBM} induced by the SBM bilinear form; this requires only localized adjustments to the definition of the norm and straightforward verification that it remains non-degenerate, preserving the qualitative coercivity conclusions without altering the global proof architecture.
